title: Which place is the 6 in?
text: Reading to the right of the decimal point, the first place is tenths and the second is hundredths. In $$3.64$$ the 6 is the first digit after the point. A common mistake is to say the 6 is worth 6 hundredths, or worth 6 ones. The 6 is in which place?

title: Turn the place into a value
text: One tenth is $$0.1$$. Six of those is $$6 \times 0.1$$. What is that value?

title: Worked solution
text: The digit 6 in $$3.64$$ is in the tenths place, so its value is $$0.6$$. The 4 is worth $$0.04$$, and the 3 is worth 3. Common mistake: reading every digit after the decimal as hundredths. General rule: the first place to the right of the decimal is tenths ($$10^{-1}$$), then hundredths ($$10^{-2}$$).
